subject: how to aggregate predictions from hiarchiarchial model within nimble code

messages.author: 8aaac405ce0daa2d
messages.subject: how to aggregate predictions from hiarchiarchial model within nimble code
parts:
Hi,

I want to predict probabilities of a binary outcome from a hierarchical model for combinations of strata: Ex. I have 6 variables, and I want to get predictions for stratifications of 4 the variables and average over 2 variables I am not interested in getting predictions for.

In R, I would set a for loop for the strata I am interested in, and the take mean predictions within those strata across all of the values for the variables I am not interested in. I am getting errors that say that I random vectors can only be indexed by scalars. 

The for loop would look something like below. I want predictions for all strata from zip, age, eth, and male and I want the mean predictions over income and education variables  

x <- numeric(6*2) # numeric vector for temporary storage of predictions
   for (i_zip in 1:N_zip){
    for (i_age in 1:N_age){
      for (i_eth in 1:N_eth){
        for (i_male in 1:N_male){
          for (i_income in 1:6){
            for (i_edu in 1:2){
               
                # collect predictions  
               x[(((i_income-1)*2) + ((i_edu-1)) + 1)] <- 
              ilogit(b[1] + b[2] * (i_male-1) +  b[3] * x_zip_hisp[i_zip] + 
                       a_zip[i_zip] + a_eth[i_eth] + a_age[i_age] +
                       a_income[i_income] + a_edu[i_edu]
                     )
            }
           }
           # take mean across income/edu for strata of interest
           p_pop[count_index[i_zip, i_age, i_eth, i_male]] <- mean(x)
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
Does anyone have ideas for how I can do this? 

I tried returning the predictions for all strata and getting the predictions I needed post-estimation, but doing it this way results in nimble output objects that are huge (several 
GBs) and too large for me to save to disk.

Best,

Cam

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: how to aggregate predictions from hiarchiarchial model within nimble code
parts:
Hi Cam,

Thanks for the question.  I think there are a couple of issues and ways to approach this.

I am not sure, but your code as written looks imperative (typical programming), but the model language is declarative.  What that means is you can't re-use the same elements of x in the innermost 2 loops.  I am not sure why you got exactly that error message and would need to see a more complete (including call to nimbleModel) or fully reproducible example to track that down, but a good starting point is avoiding re-use of x.  

Here is a way you could do it without the income and education loops, so p_pop is declared at the innermost of the first four loops:

p_pop[count_index[i_zip, i_age, i_eth, i_male]] <- average_over_income_edu(b[1] + b[2] * (i_male-1) +  b[3] * x_zip_hisp[i_zip] +  a_zip[i_zip] + a_eth[i_eth] + a_age[i_age], a_income[1:6], a_edu[1:2])

where outside of the model you write:

average_over_income_edu <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function( other_terms = double(), a_income = double(1), a_edu = double(1)) {
  ans <- 0
for(i in 1:length(a_income)) {
  for(j in 1:length(a_edu)) {
   ans <- ans + expit(other_terms + a_income[i] + a_edu[j])
  }
} 
ans <-, ans / (length(a_income) * length(a_edu))
return(ans)
returnType(double())
}

What this is doing is moving the non-declarative processing you need outside of the model.

Another option to mention is that there is a second set of monitors, with their own thinning interval, available in the MCMC.  You can set monitors2 to the predictions you need and use a larger thinning interval (thin2) than you might want for the main model parameters.  That way you'd get a smaller data structure.

I hope that helps.  Let us know more questions.

-Perry
